So when I arrived in that unit, I had to retrain the personnel so that they could respond to the requirements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you manage to improve the situation in your company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was the attitude of the reservists towards the officers who came to the brigade from the Bileca reserve officers school?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, already in peacetime, we officers who worked at the infantry reserve officers training school had a certain image, so believe me, they stood in awe of us in terms of the requests and requirements that we had for work, order, and discipline. So it was a high level of respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the period between your takeover of the company and until the end of December, what would be your assessment of the discipline in your company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In my company, I believe the discipline was at the required level, that is to say, in accordance with the tasks that we received from our superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about fire discipline within your company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. We are professionals and we respect the orders of our superior officer. So there could not be any opening of fire without dire necessity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the period from October to December 1991, the members of the reserve personnel from your company, were they sent on leave from your unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us: How were reservists sent on leave?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This was planned for the reservists who were within my company. I personally made these lists and I decided who would go on leave from all of my subordinate units. This was usually up to 48 hours, mostly exception -- and only exceptionally until 72 -- for 72 hours. Every reservist had to leave weapons, ammunition that had been issued to them at the company station for supplies, and then this would be done in an organised fashion by a TAM motor vehicle that was within the company. Then they would go under the command of one officer to Trebinje. And then these soldiers, these reservists, would go home to take a bath, to take care of their personal engagements, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us: Could a soldier from your company take anything from the positions where the unit was at the time when they would go on leave?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Only quartermaster's equipment, that is to say, a blouse, sweater, what they would take home to be washed or a washed one that would be replaced. All the other equipment had to remain within the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When reservists went on this leave that you referred to just now from your unit, was fire opened as they were leaving the positions of the unit and as they were going on leave?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He they could not open fire, because weapons remained in the unit, that is to say, that they went without any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I suggest that we pause at this point and continue tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Stojanovic, I must ask you to return tomorrow morning. We will be continuing at 9.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of July, 2004, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
